provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: high — exploitation of internet-facing CMS/Exchange/ColdFusion is a strong detection surface: web-server/WAF logs, anomalous POSTs to CMS endpoints, exploit signatures for the named CVEs, and new DLL/script artifacts written into the web root and ASP.NET temporary-files tree

high — new App_Web_*.dll modules and web-shell files appearing in the Umbraco/ASP.NET temporary-files tree, w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe/powershell, and web-shell request patterns are high-fidelity file-integrity and process-lineage detections

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — cmd.exe/batch execution spawned by the IIS worker process (w3wp.exe) and ping-sweep loops writing enumeration output are detectable via process command-line and process-lineage telemetry
medium — service-based execution (services.exe spawning an unusual image) is detectable via service-install and process-lineage telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
detection_candidates.rationale: high — new service creation (Event ID 7045) named WinStore pointing at a non-standard binary path is a high-fidelity, actor-relevant detection

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — creation of an HKCU...\Run value named WinStore referencing a payload in an unusual path is directly observable via registry-modification telemetry (Sysmon EID 13)

high — a signed binary loading an unsigned VERSION.dll/datast.dll from c:\Windows\branding\data or c:\Users\Public\Music\data is detectable via module-load (Sysmon EID 7) signature-mismatch and path-anomaly analytics; the exact DLL names/paths are actor-specific IOCs
medium — colorcpl.exe spawned with an unusual argument and hosting injected code / making network connections is detectable via process-lineage and cross-process injection (Sysmon EID 8/10) telemetry
medium — anomalous network/behavior from colorcpl.exe and injected-thread indicators are detectable with EDR, but generic injection needs correlation with the side-load event

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — high-entropy encrypted blobs embedded in DLLs and multi-layer Base64 web-shell payloads are detectable via file-entropy/YARA scanning, but require dedicated inspection

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — legitimate-looking names (WinStore, VERSION.dll) in unusual paths are detectable via name/path/hash baselining and signature-vs-name mismatch
medium — tampering with or bypassing security tooling is detectable via EDR tamper-protection and security-product health telemetry, but the report gives limited specifics
high — process access to lsass.exe and mimikatz signatures/command lines are highly observable via EDR process-access (Sysmon EID 10) telemetry
medium — Fscan execution and internal connection-fanout/port-scan bursts are detectable via process command-line and east-west network analytics
medium — scripted ping-sweep loops (repeated ping.exe invocations) and output redirection are detectable via process command-line telemetry within a recon-burst window
medium — queries listing AV/EDR services and products are detectable via command-line and API-call telemetry, though common in admin activity
medium — internal exploitation attempts surface via service crash/anomaly telemetry and east-west IDS, but require internal instrumentation
medium — admin-share access (ADMIN$/C$) and remote file writes/service installs are detectable via Type-3 logons (4624), 5140 share access and 7045 service-install events
medium — Neo-reGeorg tunneling shows as anomalous web-server child processes and SOCKS-over-HTTP request patterns; detectable via web-shell/process analytics and proxy-behavior heuristics
medium — FRP/reverse-proxy client execution and persistent outbound tunnels are detectable via process signatures and long-lived/anomalous egress connection analytics

high — outbound HTTPS from an unusual process (injected colorcpl.exe) to blog.techmersion[.]com / techmersion[.]com is detectable via proxy/DNS and process-to-network correlation; the C2 domain is an explicit IOC
medium — TLS C2 blends with legitimate HTTPS; detectable mainly via JA3/JA4 fingerprinting, destination-domain reputation and process-to-network anomaly correlation
high — files written to disk by the IIS worker process (w3wp.exe) or injected process following network transfer are detectable via file-creation and process-to-network telemetry
medium — archive-utility execution producing large/compressed outputs before egress is detectable via process command-line and file-write telemetry
medium — outbound data volume anomalies over the C2 channel to the actor domain are detectable via egress-volume analytics and process-to-network correlation

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — pre-compromise scanning of public-facing servers happens off-victim/at the perimeter and rarely attributes to this actor; hunt/external-attack-surface candidate
low — adversary domain registration/staging is off-victim; intel/infrastructure-tracking candidate (pivot on registrant/hosting/TLS)
low — capability development is off-victim; intel candidate. Downstream implant execution is where host detection lands
low — direct native-API use is generic and hard to isolate without deep memory/EDR telemetry; hunt candidate correlated with side-load and injection events
low — in-memory decode routines leave little discrete host signal; hunt candidate alongside side-load/injection correlation

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Hide Artifacts: Hidden Files and Directories
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — payloads tucked into uncommon data folders evade casual review; hunt candidate via file-creation telemetry on non-standard directories
low — post-op cleanup/file deletion is hard to observe after the fact; hunt candidate via file-deletion auditing and shell-history reconstruction
low — system-info enumeration is common and noisy; hunt candidate within a tight recon-burst process-lineage window
low — ipconfig/route/arp-style enumeration is ubiquitous; hunt candidate only in recon-burst context
low — writing enumeration output/staging files is low-signal; hunt candidate via file-creation patterns in staging directories
